node.label: Ann Laura Stoler
node.date_label: 'Tensions of Empire' (with Cooper) 1989 · Race and the Education of Desire 1995 · Tensions of Empire 1997 · 'Tense and Tender Ties' 2001 · 'Colonial Archives and the Arts of Governance' 2002 · Carnal Knowledge and Imperial Power 2002 · Haunted by Empire 2006 · Along the Archival Grain 2009 · Imperial Debris 2013 · Duress 2016
node.description: An American anthropologist of Dutch and French colonial rule who moved from Sumatra's plantation belt to the colonial archive itself. With Frederick Cooper she set an agenda for reading metropole and colony together (1989; 1997). Race and the Education of Desire (1995) questioned race and empire in Foucault's history of sexuality; Carnal Knowledge and Imperial Power (2002) asked why 'Foucault's elusive and suggestive treatment of race still remains so marginal to what colonial historians take from him' (p. 141) and treated 'colonizer/colonized' as 'a historically shifting pair of social categories that needs to be explained' (p. 13; both as quoted by Ottevaere, 2004). 'Colonial Archives and the Arts of Governance' (2002) asked scholars to move 'from archive-as-source to archive-as-subject'; Along the Archival Grain (2009) read Dutch records 'along the grain' for 'the pulse of the archive' (p. 35, as quoted by Schulte Nordholt) and 'the habits of the colonial heart' (p. 53, as quoted by Gouda). Imperial Debris (2013) and Duress (2016) turned to ruination and 'imperial durabilities'. Gouda: in postcolonial studies 'paying homage to Ann Stoler's work has become de rigueur' (2009).
node.representative_figures_and_works: Ann Laura Stoler (b. 1949); Capitalism and Confrontation in Sumatra's Plantation Belt, 1870–1979 (1985); with Frederick Cooper, 'Tensions of Empire' (American Ethnologist, 1989) and Tensions of Empire (eds, 1997); Race and the Education of Desire (1995); 'Tense and Tender Ties' (JAH, 2001); 'Colonial Archives and the Arts of Governance' (Archival Science, 2002); Carnal Knowledge and Imperial Power (2002; 2nd ed. 2010); ed., Haunted by Empire (2006); with McGranahan and Perdue, eds, Imperial Formations (2007); Along the Archival Grain (2009); ed., Imperial Debris (2013); Duress (2016); Interior Frontiers (2022). Readers: Dawn Ottevaere (2004); Frances Gouda, Remco Raben, Henk Schulte Nordholt (2009); Ronald Schultz (2015).
node.scope_note: Read on 2026-10-23 (data/extension-2026/period4-wave1-2026-10-23/evidence-archive.md §§1–2, 6): the abstract and reference list of the 2002 Archival Science essay; the contents of Along the Archival Grain and three reviews from the Bijdragen debate (Gouda and Schulte Nordholt in full, Raben's first page) with the first paragraph of Stoler's reply; Ottevaere's H-Net review of Carnal Knowledge (in full) and the UC Press contents; Schultz's H-Net review of Imperial Debris (in full); the Duke pages for Haunted by Empire and Duress. Unread: every book's body, the 2002 essay's body, 'Tense and Tender Ties' (2001), the Cooper–Stoler introductions of 1989 and 1997 (metadata and contents only, as the graph already records), Imperial Formations (2007), Interior Frontiers (2022), and Stoler's reply to her Dutch critics beyond its opening. Her 2002 notes cite Trouillot's Silencing the Past three times; no sentence of hers on Trouillot was read. Quotations from the 2009 book are 'as quoted by' Gouda or Schulte Nordholt, from Carnal Knowledge 'as quoted by' Ottevaere, from Imperial Debris 'as quoted by' Schultz, with their page numbers. Wikidata Q16203101 checked by QLever on 2026-10-23 (born 1949; anthropologist, historian; VIAF 263247736). Posts from the New School's pages (search rendering; the page itself returned 429) and the UC Press author line; the Wisconsin years (1983–89) and degrees (Barnard BA 1972, Columbia PhD 1982) from Wikipedia's citation of New School pages, orientation only; the 1985 book is not dated as an event because no publisher page was fetched. History PhD citation graph (release 2026-10-23): cited by 10.7% of Canada + US theses in 2020–25, the strongest riser of 2015–25, in 11 of 18 fields; Along the Archival Grain 4.4% and Carnal Knowledge 3.8% of theses 2015–25 (figures for this note, not for arrows).

proposed_edges.relationship: Asked colonial studies to move 'from archive-as-source to archive-as-subject' and from 'extractive' to 'ethnographic' archival work (2002); read the Dutch colonial archive 'along the grain' for 'the pulse of the archive' and set out 'to set a new standard for an ethnography of the archives' (2009, pp. 35, 45, as quoted by Schulte Nordholt)
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Own words: the 2002 abstract (read); the 2009 book's pp. 32–33, 35 and 45 as quoted by Schulte Nordholt (read in full), and pp. 3, 5, 24, 41, 43, 53 as quoted by Gouda (read in full). Both books unread. data/extension-2026/period4-wave1-2026-10-23/evidence-archive.md §§1–2.

proposed_edges.relationship: With Cooper, an agenda for reading metropole and colony together (1989; 1997); Carnal Knowledge argued that 'students of colonialism, anthropologists in particular, have taken the politically constructed dichotomy colonizer/colonized as a given rather than as a historically shifting pair of social categories' (2002, p. 13, as quoted by Ottevaere, 2004); Gouda: homage to her work 'has become de rigueur' in postcolonial studies
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Ottevaere 2004 (read in full), quoting pp. 9, 13 and 15; Gouda 2009, pp. 553–554 (read); Crossref for the 1989 introduction; the graph's existing record of Tensions of Empire (contents). The 1989 and 1997 introductions are unread. The post entry's strands colonial_intimacies and metropole_colony already name her.

proposed_edges.relationship: 'Carnal Knowledge and Imperial Power: Gender and Morality in the Making of Race' (ch. 3, 2002): 'Ethnographies of empire should attend both to changing sensibilities and to sex, to racialized regimes that were realized on a macro and micro scale' (p. 78, as quoted by Ottevaere, 2004); métissage as 'the tension between a form of authority simultaneously predicated on incorporating and distancing' (p. 83, as quoted by Ottevaere); 'Like Joan Scott', she evaluates 'historically designated categories' (Ottevaere)
proposed_edges.map_label: Gender in the making of race, 2002
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Ottevaere 2004 (read in full), quoting pp. 78 and 83 and making the Scott comparison; UC Press contents (read). Chapter unread.

proposed_edges.relationship: 'An ethnography of the archives' as a standard for the discipline (2009, p. 45, as quoted by Schulte Nordholt), against 'doing an ethnography in the archives'; her 2002 complaint that anthropologists' 'archival activity tends to remain more an extractive than an ethnographic one'; Schulte Nordholt: good historians 'are less often accustomed to making archives into an object of ethnographic research'
proposed_edges.map_label: Ethnography of, not in, the archive, 2002–09
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Stoler 2002 abstract (read); Schulte Nordholt 2009, pp. 560–562 (read in full).

proposed_edges.relationship: 'Memory-Work in Java: A Cautionary Tale' (2002, ch. 7) 'situates memories of domestic service by those who served against the density of the archives around them' (p. 162) and 'invites more work on colonial memory itself while making the "colonial" a subject rather than an assumed category of analysis' (p. 203, as quoted by Ottevaere)
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Ottevaere 2004 (read in full), quoting pp. 162 and 203; UC Press contents (read). Chapter unread.

proposed_edges.relationship: 'Tense and Tender Ties: The Politics of Comparison in North American History and (Post) Colonial Studies' (JAH 2001; Haunted by Empire, 2006) brought postcolonial critiques to North American history and questioned the conventions of comparison (Duke description); Imperial Debris (2013) asked colonial scholars 'to move beyond the theoretical and empirical limitations of postcolonial and subaltern studies' toward ongoing 'ruination' (Schultz)
proposed_edges.map_label: The politics of comparison and ruination, 2001–16
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Duke page for Haunted by Empire (contents and description, read); Crossref for the 2001 article; Schultz 2015 (read in full), quoting 'violent verb' (p. 7) and 'what people are left with' (p. 9); Duke page for Duress (contents: 'On Degrees of Imperial Sovereignty'). Bodies unread; the comparison claim rests on a publisher description.
